title_en: The Story of the Old Bridge
summary_en: A grandfather tells his grandchild how a flood swept away the village's only bridge fifty years ago — and how the whole village, pooling money, labor, and eighteen-year-old hands, built a stronger one in its place.

sentences.zh: 每年夏天，爷爷都会带着我去河边的那座老桥散步。
sentences.en: Every summer, grandfather takes me for a walk by the old bridge near the river.

sentences.zh: 桥的一边，有一排刻在石头上的名字，太老了，有些已经很难看清楚了。
sentences.en: On one side of the bridge, there is a row of names carved into the stone, so old that some are hard to read clearly.

sentences.zh: 我有一次问爷爷，那些是谁的名字，他笑着说：“继续走，我给你讲完这个故事。”
sentences.en: I once asked grandfather whose names those were — he smiled and said, "Keep walking, and I'll tell you the whole story."

sentences.zh: 那座桥看起来很普通，可是爷爷说，它的故事一点也不普通。
sentences.en: The bridge looks very ordinary, but grandfather says its story isn't ordinary at all.

sentences.zh: 五十年前，村子里还没有这座桥，大家过河都要坐船。
sentences.en: Fifty years ago, the village didn't have this bridge yet, and everyone had to take a boat to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 后来，村里的年轻人一起出钱出力，建了第一座木桥。
sentences.en: Later, the village's young people pooled money and effort, and built the first wooden bridge.

sentences.zh: 那座桥不大，但是方便多了，大家都很高兴。
sentences.en: That bridge wasn't big, but it was much more convenient, and everyone was very happy.

sentences.zh: 可是有一年夏天，连续下了好几天大雨。
sentences.en: But one summer, it rained heavily for several days in a row.

sentences.zh: 河水越涨越高，最后把那座木桥冲走了。
sentences.en: The river water rose higher and higher, and finally swept the wooden bridge away.

sentences.zh: 爷爷至今还记得木桥断的时候发出的声音，那一声巨响传遍了整个山谷。
sentences.en: Grandfather still remembers the sound the wooden bridge made as it broke — a crack that echoed across the whole valley.

sentences.zh: 没有了桥，孩子们没办法去河对岸上学，很多人也没办法去市场卖东西。
sentences.en: Without the bridge, children had no way to cross to school, and many people had no way to get to market to sell things.

sentences.zh: 爷爷说，那段时间，全村人都很着急。
sentences.en: Grandfather said that during that time, the whole village was very anxious.

sentences.zh: 村长决定，这一次要建一座更坚固的石桥，不能再被大水冲走。
sentences.en: The village head decided that this time they would build a sturdier stone bridge, one that couldn't be swept away by floodwater again.

sentences.zh: 可是建石桥需要很多钱，村里哪有那么多钱？
sentences.en: But building a stone bridge needed a lot of money — where would the village get that much?

sentences.zh: 没想到，村里几乎每一家都拿出了自己的一点积蓄。
sentences.en: Unexpectedly, almost every family in the village contributed a bit of their own savings.

sentences.zh: 年轻人去山上搬石头，老人在家做饭，照顾孩子。
sentences.en: Young people went up the mountain to carry stones, while elders stayed home cooking and watching the children.

sentences.zh: 大家分工合作，整整忙了三个月。
sentences.en: Everyone divided the work and cooperated, and stayed busy for a full three months.

sentences.zh: 他说，有一个下午，他搬着一块石头走过河上的一块窄木板的时候，脚一滑，有一秒钟，他以为自己要直接掉进水里了。
sentences.en: He said that one afternoon, carrying a stone across a narrow wooden plank laid over the river, he slipped — and for one terrifying second, thought he would fall straight into the water.

sentences.zh: 幸好，后面的两个村民及时拉住了他的手臂，石头自己掉进了河里，发出很大的水声，但是他没事。
sentences.en: Luckily, two fellow villagers behind him caught his arm in time, and the stone fell into the river alone, with a loud splash — but he was fine.

sentences.zh: 爷爷说，他当年才十八岁，也每天去河边搬石头。
sentences.en: Grandfather said he was only eighteen that year, and he too went to the riverside every day to carry stones.

sentences.zh: 石桥建好那天，全村人都来了，大家放鞭炮庆祝。
sentences.en: The day the stone bridge was finished, the whole village came, and everyone set off firecrackers to celebrate.

sentences.zh: 从那以后，五十年过去了，这座桥一直都很坚固，从来没有被大水冲走过。
sentences.en: Since then, fifty years have passed, and the bridge has always stayed sturdy, never once swept away by floodwater.

sentences.zh: 爷爷常说，这座桥不只是一座桥，也是全村人团结的证明。
sentences.en: Grandfather often says this bridge isn't just a bridge — it's also proof of the whole village's unity.

sentences.zh: 我终于问他，石头上刻的到底是谁的名字，他说，那是当年每一家出钱的人，这样就没有人会忘记大家一起建成的东西。
sentences.en: I finally asked him whose names were carved into the stone — he said they were every family that gave money that year, so no one would ever forget what they had built together.

sentences.zh: 我每次走过这座桥，都会想起爷爷讲的这个故事。
sentences.en: Every time I walk across this bridge, I think of this story grandfather told.

grammar_points.explanation_en: "The more A, the more B" — both clauses track a quantity rising together. 越涨越高 is "rose and rose, getting higher and higher".
grammar_points.example_en: The rain fell harder and harder.

grammar_points.explanation_en: 冲走 ("swept away") takes 把 to front its object, since it describes something being done TO the bridge, not the water doing something general.
grammar_points.example_en: The strong wind blew the tree down.

grammar_points.explanation_en: "Not only A, but also B" — reframes something as carrying a second, often deeper, meaning beyond its obvious one.
grammar_points.example_zh: 这不只是一个故事，也是一段历史。
grammar_points.example_en: This isn't just a story — it's also a piece of history.

questions.q_zh: 第一座桥是什么时候建的？后来发生了什么？
questions.q_en: When was the first bridge built, and what happened to it later?
questions.answer_en: Young villagers built a wooden bridge; years later, a flood swept it away.

questions.q_zh: 村里人是怎么一起建成石桥的？
questions.q_en: How did the villagers build the stone bridge together?
questions.answer_en: Almost every family contributed savings; young people carried stone from the mountain while elders cooked and watched the children, and it took three months.

questions.q_zh: 爷爷说这座桥代表什么？
questions.q_en: What does grandfather say the bridge represents?
questions.answer_en: Not just a bridge, but proof of the whole village's unity.
